query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases? Earlier studies of refractory and transition-metal-based high-entropy alloys primarily examined elemental and compositional effects involving Al, Cr, Si, Ti, and V, but the reported outcomes depended on composition limits, phase readjustment, and processing. This emphasis has not resolved the oxidation behavior of compositionally complex alloys, for which synergistic elemental effects make interpretation difficult. The starting alloy was designed to retain an fcc matrix for formability and has demonstrated notable strength and fatigue performance, so any explanation should account for its integrity without compromising those constraints. Define a controlled comparison that would distinguish the proposed explanation, predict observations relative to the starting-state baseline, identify applicable exposure boundaries and supporting prior evidence, and state an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: At 700–900 °C the dominant degradation mechanism of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 (fcc) HEA is selective outward diffusion of Al and Ti that nucleates a duplex Al-Ti-rich oxide layer (Al2O3 + TiO2/spinel) whose local growth depletes the adjacent matrix of Al and Ti; the resulting Al(Ti)-poor zones lose solid-solution strengthening and promote Cr segregation and Cr-rich grain-boundary oxidation. In reducing (H2) atmospheres the external Al-Ti oxide is destabilized, driving sub-surface internal oxidation of Ti that forms nano-voided Ti-oxides and accelerates grain-boundary embrittlement. Hence the coupling of fast Al/Ti diffusion with their higher oxygen affinity, not the absolute Cr level, governs high-temperature degradation in either oxidizing or reducing gases.
generation.material_initial_state: Laser-powder bed fusion (LPBF) Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy in the as-built or homogenized condition with a single-phase fcc matrix, ~0.5 µm equiaxed solidification cells and ∑3 twin density typical of AM processing; room-temperature yield strength ≈ 900 MPa and fatigue limit ≈ 350 MPa.
generation.intervention: Expose coupons to 800 °C for 100 h either in (i) dry air (21 % O2) or (ii) 5 % H2 + 95 % N2 (reducing). Compare with compositionally identical coupons in which Al and Ti outward diffusion is suppressed by a 2 µm sputtered Cr layer prior to exposure.
generation.conditions: Temperature 800 ± 10 °C; total pressure 1 atm; gas flow 100 sccm to minimize boundary-layer effects; samples cooled in inert Ar to avoid post-exposure oxidation.
generation.structural_mediator: Al/Ti concentration gradients that develop across the first 1–3 µm from the surface and associated duplex Al-Ti oxide layer thickness.
generation.mechanism: 1. High Al and Ti chemical potentials at the surface drive outward lattice diffusion (short-circuit along LPBF cell boundaries/twins). 2. Al and Ti react preferentially with O2 to form Al2O3 and TiO2 or Al-Ti spinel, consuming local Al/Ti. 3. Resulting depletion zone lowers local solid-solution strength and raises Cr activity, leading to Cr-rich grain-boundary oxides. 4. In H2, the external Al-Ti oxide lacks thermodynamic stability; O activity is reduced, shifting oxidation internally where TiO2 precipitates generate nano-voids, causing embrittlement.
generation.predicted_outcome: Baseline coupons will: (a) in air – form a continuous 1–3 µm Al-Ti oxide scale with an underlying 0.5–1 µm Al/Ti-depleted zone and intergranular Cr-rich oxides; room-temperature tensile ductility decreases by ≥25 % while yield strength drops ≤10 %. (b) in H2 – show discontinuous external oxides, but a 3–5 µm sub-surface Ti-oxide/void band and ≥40 % ductility loss. Cr-coated coupons will suppress Al/Ti outward diffusion, show negligible depletion or internal oxidation, retain ≥90 % of baseline ductility/strength in both atmospheres.
generation.baseline: As-built alloy before exposure: no surface oxide thicker than native ~5 nm Al-rich layer; homogeneous Al and Ti distribution in first micron; tensile elongation 14 %, YS 900 MPa.
generation.boundary: Valid for 700–900 °C, exposures ≤10^2 h, oxygen partial pressure from 10^−20 atm (5 % H2/N2) up to 0.21 atm (air); fails outside if molten phases form (>1200 °C) or if Al/Ti content varies by >±0.1 at. fraction.
generation.uncertainty: No direct prior data on this specific AM fcc HEA; oxidation/diffusion kinetics inferred from binary oxides and reported Al-Cr-Ti effects in related HEAs. Quantitative scale thicknesses and mechanical property losses could vary ±50 %.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare four sets of LPBF coupons: (1) baseline–air, (2) baseline–H2, (3) Cr-coated–air, (4) Cr-coated–H2. Expose at 800 °C for 100 h. Perform cross-sectional STEM/EDS for Al, Ti, Cr profiles; measure oxide scale thickness and location; quantify room-temperature tensile properties.
measurements: Al, Ti, Cr concentration vs depth (SIMS or STEM-EDS)
Oxide phase identification and thickness (XRD, TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if (a) Al/Ti depletion <0.2 at.% across first micron while significant degradation occurs, or (b) Cr coating fails to mitigate degradation despite suppressing Al/Ti outward diffusion, or (c) dominant internal oxidation products are not Ti-oxides but Cr- or Fe-oxides.
